status_update.description: Manus is working on your request

assistant_message.content:
Done — the full breakdown for Marc is ready: **Marc_Portal_Breakdown_and_Development_Value.md** (attached).

**What's in it:**

**Part 1 — The OneSite & Yardi Reporting Portal.** I pulled the complete history from your referenced task and the archived original project (947 events), and broke the portal down into what it actually is: eight coordinated subsystems (responsive multi-user web portal, live 310-report catalog sync, property directory sync, request workflow engine with Select-All preflight, a self-hosted GitHub Actions runner driving a live Edge session, an idempotent filing pipeline, a report library with PDF/Excel/HTML viewers, and the Manager's Checklist + email drafting system). It explains — in plain terms Marc can follow — why the credential-free security model, the Request #60001 reconciliation (35 selected properties vs. the 21-property companion plan, which can't be fixed by rerunning), and the Windows Edge bridge transition make this a multi-week engineering program. Market-rate estimate for the portal alone at $75/hr: **$57,000–$81,750** (760–1,090 hours).

**Part 2 — The full inventory.** 30 apps and portals pulled from your 3D portfolio's projects.json, your GitHub repos, and the live deployments — including the PropertyMax Enhanced Dashboard, Operations Hub, Vacancy Report, Investor Summary, Onboarding Portal & Admin, Training Hub, Rent Comps API (42 properties / 3,755 units), Loss to Lease, Cost Segregation, Monthly Inspections, CEO Command Center, Tasks Backup Portal, AI Recordings automation, and the rest — each with scope, live URL, hour estimate, and cost at $75/hr.

**Bottom line for Marc:** the total in-house software portfolio works out to **≈ $188,600–$279,150 (midpoint ~$234,000, roughly 3,100 hours ≈ 1.5 developer-years)** at the $75/hr floor — with BLS/freelance market calibration showing $75/hr is the low end. Part 3 frames the portal's current state as a deliberate safety gate, not a stall, and offers an in-person walkthrough of every system.

One note: your brosefolio work-index site currently returns 404, so I sourced the inventory from the 3D portfolio data file and GitHub instead — you may want to redeploy that site at some point.
